notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 05/15/2026
Patient: María Teresa Salcedo, 74-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 05/15/2026. The study evaluated the patient's sleep architecture and respiratory events throughout the night. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 31.5 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 2% of all events. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent desaturations associated with respiratory events. Sleep stages were within normal limits, with appropriate distribution of REM and non-REM sleep. The findings are consistent with moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea. Recommendations include consideration of positive airway pressure therapy and follow-up with a sleep medicine specialist for management.

notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/02/2026
Patient: María Teresa Salcedo, 74-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Ms. Salcedo has been using CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. Despite adherence, she reports persistent symptoms suggestive of inadequate control.

Physical Examination:
BMI 28.2 kg/m2.
No other significant findings noted.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 21.4 events/hour on CPAP at 10 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates suboptimal response to current CPAP settings with significant residual apnea events.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative therapies or adjustment of CPAP parameters.
2. Schedule follow-up sleep study to evaluate efficacy of any changes.
3. Continue monitoring adherence and symptomatology.
4. Educate patient on importance of follow-up and potential treatment modifications.

Summary:
Ms. Salcedo's sleep apnea remains inadequately controlled on current CPAP therapy, necessitating further evaluation and management.
